Order No. 04/Dated 20th July, 2023 Heard.

2. Admit.
3.

Mr. Shailesh Kumar Sinha, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, waives notice on behalf of the
State.
4. Call for the Lower Court Records.

5. With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the instant interlocutory application has
been heard which has been filed under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence dated
Kamal Kishore Minz @ Kamal Kishor Oraon vs The State Of Jharkhand on 20 July, 2023

1

18.05.2023 in connection with Sessions Trial No. 59 of 2021, by which the appellant has been
convicted under Sections 417 and 376(1) of Ipc and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment
for 10 years with fine of Rs.20,000/- for the offence under Section 376(1) of Ipc and in default of
payment of fine, has been further directed to undergo further imprisonment for one month and also
been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year for the offence committed under
Section 417 of Ipc with fine of Rs.5,000/- and in default of payment of fine, has been further
directed to undergo imprisonment for 10 days.

6.  This matter was heard by this Court on 05.07.2023 and on that date it was argued on behalf of the appellant by referring the testimony of PW-2, the victim, as recorded under paragraph-14 of the impugned judgment wherein the testimony of PW-2, wherein she herself has admitted that she was having physical relationship in the garb of solemnization of marriage with the appellant.

6.1 Further, the PW-3, the father of the victim, has deposed in paragraph 15 by admitting the fact in his cross-examination that there was love affair between the appellant and her daughter and the appellant used to visit his house.

6.2 Learned counsel for the appellant has argued that in view of the testimony of PW-2 and 3 as referred hereinabove that there is no ingredient of Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code against the appellant.

7. This Court, on consideration of the aforesaid submission, has called upon the State to file objection in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Somesh Chaurasia vs. State of M.P. and Anr., 2021 SCC OnLine SC 480.
8.

entities.text: Somesh Chaurasia vs. State of M.P. and Anr., 2021 SCC OnLine SC 480
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Objection in terms thereof has been filed wherein the fact about the physical relationship with consent has not been disputed.

The same also cannot be disputed since it is the version of the victim,
PW-2, corroborated by the PW-3, the father of the victim.

9. This Court, having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on consideration of the testimony of PW-2 and PW- 3, the victim and her father respectively, wherein the physical relationship has been admitted on the garb of solemnization of marriage, is prima facie of the view that it is the consensual physical relationship.
10. Therefore, this Court is of the view that prima facie case is made out in favour of the appellant.
11. Accordingly, I.A. No.4965 of 2023 stands allowed.

12. In consequence thereof, the appellant named above, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Ten Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned District and Additional Sessions Judge-I, Lohardaga in connection with Sessions Trial No. 59 of 2021.

entities.text: District and Additional Sessions Judge-I, Lohardaga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 13. It is made clear that whatever observation has been made hereinabove will not prejudice the case of the appellants on merit since the appeal is lying pending for its consideration.
